title: Forrest Preston retained ownership of Life Care Center of Skagit Valley during Q1
text:
During the first quarter of 2026, Life Care Center of Skagit Valley remained under the ownership of Forrest Preston, per data from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) . Located in Skagit County, the nursing home has belonged to Forrest Preston since Oct. 25, 1995.
Life Care Center of Skagit Valley is classified as a for-profit facility.
Throughout that period, the facility posted an overall CMS rating of two, which is below Washington’s state nursing home average of 3.3. CMS issues ratings based on wide-ranging factors, including health inspection results, staffing numbers, and the standard of care provided to residents.
The data shows Life Care Center of Skagit Valley cared for an average of 75.8 residents each day in the initial quarter of 2026, offering 150 licensed beds. The facility operates independently and does not have direct hospital affiliation.
Also, as of Q1 2026, the center received one fine totaling $35,997 and was cited for one penalty.
There were 4 for-profit nursing homes operating within Skagit County, Washington, in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the older adult demographic continues expanding while numbers among children decline. From 2020 to 2024, the U.S. population aged 65 and above grew by 13%, contrasted with a 1.7% reduction among individuals under 18. The growth among older adults over the last century is marked, from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million by 2024.
A study from 2021 estimates almost half of this age group, about 28 million, could need long-term services and supports, with projections suggesting over one-third might eventually require nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
